audience_description: A SaaS marketer or growth founder studying Preply's homepage evolution to understand how a language tutoring marketplace repositioned from aspirational lifestyle messaging to efficiency-first copy — before deciding whether to apply the same shift to their own product.
recommended_h1_format: How [Company] Rewrote Its Homepage Over 6 Years
content_angle: Focus on the observable signals that distinguish a consumer-market aspiration headline from an efficiency promise — and why the addition of 'Book a demo' to a consumer homepage is the most unexpected, and most instructive, change in this teardown.
what_the_searcher_wants: To understand whether Preply's shift from aspirational to efficiency-first messaging is worth replicating, and what specific changes they can copy or test on their own homepage.
what_to_avoid: Claiming the homepage changes drove measurable business outcomes. Do not say conversions improved, signups increased, or the positioning worked — cite only what changed and what it may signal.
